h9: Four things set your fare — nothing else.
h10: Route. Distance and drive time between your pickup and drop-off, checked against real traffic conditions for your date, not a straight-line estimate.
h11: Time of day. A 30% supplement applies between midnight and 6 a.m. — it's built into the quoted fare, never added after the ride.
h12: Wait time beyond the complimentary window. 60 minutes are included at airports and FBOs; time held beyond that is the only variable added after booking, and it's agreed with you in advance, not discovered afterward.
h13: The calendar. A handful of dates a year — Art Basel, major boat shows, F1, Ultra — put real pressure on vehicle availability across every operator in South Florida, ours included. Those dates are quoted individually, always before you confirm.
h14: That's the entire list. No membership tiers, no surge multiplier, no "premium demand" language — just the four inputs above, quoted in writing before you decide.
h17: Miami-Dade County chauffeur registration isn't a badge we bought — it's a public record. Getting one requires a background check, a clean driving record on file with the county, and annual renewal to stay active. It's issued and tracked by Miami-Dade County's Department of Transportation and Public Works, independently of anything we say about ourselves.
h18: Most operators in this market write "licensed and insured" without a number attached. We put ours in the footer of every page for one reason: it's checkable, and we'd rather you check it than take our word for it.
h20: Miami-Dade County Department of Transportation and Public Works, Passenger Transportation Regulatory Division.
h22: A confirmed fare vs. an app's estimate.
h24: The number on screen when you request is not the number when the car arrives — demand pricing can move it in either direction up to the moment of pickup.
h25: The driver and vehicle are assigned at request time, from whoever is nearest and available.
h26: Cancellations and driver reassignment are common in the minutes before pickup, especially at airports during peak arrival banks.
h28: The number you're quoted is the number you pay, agreed before the vehicle is dispatched — not adjusted in transit.
h29: The same vehicle and standard, held for your reservation specifically, not pulled from a shared pool.
h30: One phone number if a flight changes or a meeting runs long — not a support ticket.
h31: Neither model is wrong — they solve different problems. A rideshare app is built for availability at a moment's notice. A confirmed fare is built for a specific date you can't afford to leave to chance.
h33: What that looks like on your reservation.
h35: Your pickup is set by when the aircraft actually touches down — we track the flight and adjust if it's early, late, or diverted.
h37: You see the number and agree to it before a vehicle is assigned — not after the ride starts.
h39: If something goes wrong, you're calling the person who owns the outcome — not a regional support line.
h41: Reservation, cancellation, wait time, and disruptions.
h42: How does a reservation get confirmed?+
h43: You receive a fixed quote in writing before anything is booked. The reservation is confirmed once you accept that quote — vehicle and chauffeur are then held specifically for your date and time.
h44: How much complimentary wait time do I get?+
h45: 60 minutes at airports and FBOs, measured from actual landing, not the scheduled time. 15 minutes on hotel, residence, and other pickups.
h47: Free cancellation up to 2 hours before pickup. A no-show, or a cancellation inside that window without a qualifying reason (flight cancellation, medical emergency), may require prepayment or a card on file before any future booking is confirmed.
h48: What if my flight is delayed or cancelled?
h49: A delayed flight is tracked automatically and never charged extra for the wait within the complimentary window. A cancelled flight carries no charge at all — let us know as soon as you know.
h50: Is there a supplement for late-night pickups?
h51: Yes — a 30% supplement applies to pickups between midnight and 6 a.m. It's included in the fare you're quoted, not added afterward.
h52: Are your rates per person or per vehicle?
h53: Per vehicle. The fare is the same whether one passenger rides or the Suburban is full.
